articles.en: How Do Climate Scientists Make Predictions?
articles.zh: 气候科学家是怎么「算出」未来的
body: When scientists talk about the climate of the future, they are careful with their words. They rarely say prediction. They say projection instead, and the difference matters more than most people realise.
科学家谈未来气候时用词很谨慎。他们很少说「预测」，而是说「推演」，这两个词的差别比大多数人以为的要大。

A prediction claims something will happen. A projection says: if humans burn this much fuel, the planet will probably warm by this much. It is conditional. Change the human behaviour and the answer changes too.
「预测」是断言某件事一定会发生。「推演」说的是：如果人类烧掉这么多燃料，地球大概会升温这么多。它是有条件的。人的行为一变，结果也跟着变。

To build these models, researchers track how much energy the Earth absorbs versus how much it sends back to space. When those two numbers stop matching, the system is out of whack, and that gap is what drives everything else.
为了建立这些模型，研究者会追踪地球吸收了多少能量、又向太空放回去多少。当这两个数字对不上，整个系统就失衡了，而这个缺口就是后面一切变化的推手。
tips: 推演、预估（有前提条件的推算）
有条件的、取决于别的因素

articles.zh: 允许「吃药」的运动会，你敢看吗
body: Imagine a sports event where doping is not banned but openly allowed. That is exactly the idea behind the Enhanced Games, and it is fair to say the reaction has been loud.
想象一场比赛，不但不禁用兴奋剂，反而公开允许。这正是「增强运动会」的想法，可以说，外界反应非常激烈。
Supporters argue athletes already take drugs in secret, so being honest about it is safer. Critics say it sets a bad example for young people and turns sport into a chemistry competition.
支持者说，运动员本来就在偷偷用药，公开反而更安全。反对者说，这给年轻人带了坏头，把体育变成了化学比赛。
The debate is deeply divisive. Where exactly is the line between training hard and cheating? Once you normalise something, it becomes very difficult to go back.
这场争论让人严重分裂。到底哪条线之内叫刻苦训练，越过去就叫作弊？一旦一件事被当成正常，就很难再退回去了。
tips: 让某件事变得理所当然

articles.zh: 那些想当厨师的人，后来怎么样了
body: Cooking shows make professional kitchens look glamorous. In reality, most chefs work long unsocial hours in hot, noisy rooms, and the pay at the start is modest.
美食节目把专业后厨拍得光鲜。现实里，大多数厨师在又热又吵的地方长时间上班，作息还跟正常人反着，起步工资也不高。
So why do people still do it? Many say it is the only job where they can see the result of their work in minutes, and where a bad day is forgotten by the next service.
那为什么还有人做？很多人说，这是少数几种能在几分钟内看到自己成果的工作，而且今天再糟，下一轮开餐就翻篇了。
The advice from those who stayed is simple: learn the basics until they are boring, find a kitchen with a decent head chef, and do not chase fame. Skill comes first; everything else follows.
坚持下来的人给的建议很朴素：把基本功练到觉得无聊为止，找一个主厨人品还行的后厨，别追名气。手艺在前，其他的自然会来。
tips: 跟别人作息相反的上班时间

body: Dyslexia is usually described as a problem: letters move around, reading is slow, spelling is unreliable. For a child at school, it can feel like being labelled lazy when you are working twice as hard.
「读写困难」通常被当成一种毛病：字会乱跑、读得慢、拼写老出错。对一个学生来说，明明比别人多花一倍力气，却被贴上懒的标签。
But some researchers now look at it differently. People with dyslexia often think in pictures, spot patterns quickly, and are good at seeing how a whole system fits together.
但现在有些研究者换了个看法。有读写困难的人往往用画面思考，看规律很快，也擅长看清一整个系统是怎么拼起来的。
Calling it a superpower may go too far. The point is simply that a brain wired for exploring is not a broken brain — it just needs a different way in.
说它是「超能力」也许有点过了。核心意思只是：一个天生擅长探索的大脑不是坏掉的大脑，它只是需要换一个入口。

articles.zh: 在水里做体操，到底有多难
body: Artistic swimming looks effortless from the poolside: smiling faces, perfect lines, everyone moving as one. Underwater, it is a different story entirely.
在池边看花样游泳，一切都轻松自如：笑着的脸、完美的队形、所有人动作一致。水下则完全是另一回事。

Athletes hold their breath for up to a minute while upside down, kicking hard enough to lift half their body out of the water. They cannot touch the bottom, and they must stay in time with music they can barely hear.
运动员要倒立着憋气将近一分钟，同时用力打水，把半个身子撑出水面。脚不能碰池底，还得跟着几乎听不清的音乐踩点。
Perhaps the hardest part is the face. Whatever is happening below the surface, the expression above it must never give it away. That is the whole skill in one image.
也许最难的是表情。水面下不管多狼狈，水面上的那张脸都不能露出一点破绽。这一幕，就把这项运动全说清楚了。
